tickets.title: P2-116: an equity rule with NO equity reading reports EvaluatedNotEnforcing, so 88 dormant accounts read exactly like the one that is actually protected
tickets.defect:
`GuardRules.cs` counts EVIDENCE so that a rule which cannot possibly fire reports INERT instead of a reassuring green. Three rules read the account's equity and all three count the wrong thing.

They count the existence of an `AccountState` OBJECT:

    R(c.Account == null ? (double?)null : c.Account.AccountEquity,
      c.Config.PnLRules.TrailingDrawdown, c.Account == null ? 0 : 1)
                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Every subscribed account has one of those. So every account scores evidence 1 and reports `EvaluatedNotEnforcing` -- the state that means 'this rule ran and you are within it'.

MEASURED LIVE, 2026-08-15, with the broker connected and the market shut:

  Provider31 accounts subscribed .................. 89
  ...reporting any equity at all .................. 1  (TAKEPROFITPRO524207503, $50,182.75)
  ...with any per-account guard event, ever ....... 0
  `Trailing drawdown` state on all 89 ............. EvaluatedNotEnforcing, limit 1500

The funded account and a blank one are byte-identical on every row except the number:

  TAKEPROFITPRO524207503  equity=50182.75  Trailing drawdown  EvaluatedNotEnforcing  cur=50182.75  limit=1500
  TAKEPROFITPRO4945748    equity=0.0       Trailing drawdown  EvaluatedNotEnforcing  cur=0.0       limit=1500

The rule is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of firing on those 88. Trailing drawdown breaches when `currentPnL < PeakEquity - TrailingDrawdown`; with no reading `PeakEquity` stays 0 and the test is `0 < -1500`, which is never true. Confirmed from the other end: `EvaluatePnLRules` is driven by `AccountItemUpdate` and the audit log shows zero per-account events for any Provider31 account -- the enforcer has not run once.

This is `F-9`'s class in the OPTIMISTIC direction, which is the dangerous one, and it is on the one surface built specifically to answer 'is the guard actually protecting me'. An operator sees 89 rows saying the same reassuring thing and cannot tell the one account that is protected from the 88 that cannot be.
tickets.spec:
ONE FILE: `addons/GuardRules.cs`.

1. ADD A HELPER, beside `R(...)` and `Off(...)` in `GuardRuleRegistry`:

```csharp
private const string NoEquityReading =
    "this account reports no equity, so its peak equity stays 0 and the rule cannot fire";

private static bool HasEquityReading(RiskGuardAddOn.AccountStateSnapshot account)
{
    return account != null && account.AccountEquity != 0.0;
}
```

⚠️ `!= 0.0` AND NOT `> 0`. This is pinned by a test and it is the single most important line in the ticket. An account whose equity has gone NEGATIVE is reporting a reading, and it is the account most likely to be in trouble. `> 0` would switch its trailing-drawdown rule to INERT at the exact moment it matters, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed.

Put a comment above the helper recording WHY the count moved -- the object-vs-reading distinction and the 89/1 measurement -- and the `!= 0.0` reason. A future reader will otherwise 'tidy' it to `> 0`.

2. `Trailing drawdown` (ConfigPath `PnLRules.TrailingDrawdown`):
   * add `EvidenceLabel = "accounts reporting an equity reading",`
   * evidence becomes `HasEquityReading(c.Account) ? 1 : 0`
   * pass `HasEquityReading(c.Account) ? null : NoEquityReading` as the note

3. `Firm trailing drawdown` (ConfigPath `FirmMirror.TrailingDD.Amount`): a SECOND READER of the same state. It already gates evidence on the account being MAPPED to a firm -- which a dormant eval certainly can be. Mapped and unread is still unread.
   * change its EvidenceLabel from `"accounts mapped to a firm"` to `"accounts mapped to a firm and reporting an equity reading"`
   * evidence becomes `mapped && HasEquityReading(c.Account) ? 1 : 0`
   * when `mapped && !HasEquityReading(c.Account)`, PREFIX the existing `note` with `NoEquityReading + "; "`. The existing note text says which plan resolved and must not be lost -- it is the only place that says whether the numbers in force came from the plan or the fallback block.

   ⚠️ DO NOT touch `Firm daily loss` directly below it. It carries the SAME EvidenceLabel string today and reads `RealizedPnL`, not equity. Its label stays exactly as it is.

4. `Peak equity giveback` (ConfigPath `PropFirm.EnablePeakEquityProtection`): the third site. It reports no CurrentValue, so it looks unlike the other two -- but the enforcer behind it tracks peak equity, and with no reading the peak stays 0 and the giveback can never trigger. What a row DISPLAYS is not what decides whether it can fire.
   * add `EvidenceLabel = "accounts reporting an equity reading",`
   * evidence becomes `HasEquityReading(c.Account) ? 1 : 0`
   * PREFIX the existing `"ignores peaks below $... (P1-40)"` note with `NoEquityReading + "; "` when there is no reading. Keep the P1-40 text in both branches.

NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. `DeriveState` already maps `EvidenceCount <= 0` to `Inert`; you do not touch it. No new public members, no signature changes, no new parameters.
tickets.context:
SCOPE, AND IT IS PINNED BY A TEST THAT IS GREEN RIGHT NOW.

Do NOT widen this to every per-account rule. `Daily loss limit`, `Max trades per session` and `Max contracts per account` all use `c.Account == null ? 0 : 1` and all three MUST keep reporting Enforcing for an account with no equity reading. The reason is that the two kinds of number are different IN KIND:

  * `RealizedPnL` is tracked by the GUARD ITSELF from `AccountItemUpdate`. Zero there is a legitimate reading for a flat account and cannot be distinguished from 'never reported'.
  * `AccountEquity` is a number the BROKER pushes and the guard passively reads. 0.0 is exactly what 'never pushed' looks like.

Reporting a flat, funded, actively watched account as INERT on its daily loss limit is the same defect in the PESSIMISTIC direction, and an operator who learns to ignore INERT rows has lost the signal the whole registry exists to give them. `TestP2116_TheRealizedPnLRulesAreDeliberatelyLeftAlone` fails if you widen it.

WHY A LABEL IS REQUIRED AND NOT OPTIONAL. `EvidenceLabel == null` is a declaration that the rule is SCALAR -- its input is a number that is always present, so it never goes INERT. A rule that CAN go inert without a label hands the operator a red row with no noun in it, and the classification is derived by sweep rather than trusted: `TestP2116_EquityBackedRulesAreFoundBySweepNotByHand` moves ONLY the account's equity and demands a label from every rule whose evidence follows it. There is nowhere to hide and nothing to hand-maintain.

WHY INERT AND NOT A NEW STATE. INERT already means exactly this -- 'the evaluator ran and its evidence set is empty, so the verdict is a foregone conclusion'. It is `P2-25`'s state, the one every static check misses. And it SELF-HEALS: the moment the broker pushes a number the row goes green on its own, with no operator action and no config change.

WHY THE NOTE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE STATE. `P2-113`: a registry that records WHY a rule is unevaluated inherits the obligation to say so, and its reason went on being served for two days after it stopped being true. A red row that does not name the missing reading makes the next reader re-derive this entire investigation.

COUNTING THE SITES IS THE POINT. Three readers of the same state, and the whole reason two of them are in this ticket rather than a later one is that this codebase's most repeated defect -- `P1-100`, `P2-98`/`P1-99`, `P1-105` -- is a predicate learning a clause that the OTHER readers of the same state never do.

THE AUTHOR ALREADY KNEW THIS CLASS AND APPLIED IT EIGHT LINES BELOW. The aggregate contract cap carries `EvidenceLabel = "accounts visible to the aggregate cap"` and the comment 'An aggregate cap over ZERO known accounts is not enforcing anything, and would otherwise read as green.' The identical reasoning was simply never carried to the equity rules.
expect_green: trailing drawdown on an account reporting NO equity is INERT
the note on an unreadable account names the missing EQUITY reading
a firm-MAPPED account reporting no equity is INERT on the firm trailing drawdown
peak equity giveback on an account reporting no equity is INERT
at least one rule's evidence follows the account's equity reading
tickets.note_expect_green:
All five were VERIFIED red at the 1931/5 baseline -- expect_green is matched against the runner's FAILURE LINES and means red-now-green-after.

THREE MORE ASSERTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS LIST because they are GREEN NOW and must STAY green. They are not filler; each one refuses a specific wrong fix, and a wrong fix passes all five listed assertions above:

  * `TestP2116_AnAccountWithAnEquityReadingStillEnforces` -- the negative control. A rule that reports INERT for everything satisfies every listed assertion. `P3-30`'s audit shipped behind three positive-only acceptance tests and fired on correctly protected accounts.
  * `TestP2116_ANegativeEquityIsAReadingNotAnAbsence` -- refuses `> 0`.
  * `TestP2116_TheRealizedPnLRulesAreDeliberatelyLeftAlone` -- refuses widening the fix to every per-account rule.

The existing `TestUi3_AnEmptyCollectionCanNeverReportEnforcing` was amended in the same commit as these tests, so that evidence backed by an account READING is classified alongside evidence backed by a COLLECTION. Without that amendment the honest new label would have read as 'has a label but never varies' and the gate would have fired on the fix rather than on a defect. You do not need to do anything about it; it is already green and stays green.
